SUMMARY

Intercontinental Exchange, Inc.(ICE+5.34%)reported financial results for the third quarter of 2026, highlighted by growth in recurring and transaction revenues across varied market conditions. Management reported that the company’s business model remained effective through periods of acute and receding volatility as well as shifting geopolitical risks. The company’s strategy involved expanding its multi-asset class offerings, integrating mortgage technology solutions, and investing in blockchain-based retail market infrastructure. Management indicated that they are focusing on leveraging proprietary data and network effects to serve institutional risk management and evolving retail trading demands.

Operator:Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and welcome to today's ICE Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Conference Call and Webcast. After today's prepared remarks, we will host a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one to raise your hand. To withdraw your question, press star one again. I will now hand the conference over to Steve Egerton. Steve, please go ahead.

Steve Egerton:Good morning. ICE's third quarter 2026 earnings release and presentation can be found in the Investor section of ice.com. These items will be archived, and our call will be available for replay. Today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements, which we undertake no obligation to update, represent our current judgment and are subject to risks, assumptions, and uncertainties. For a description of the risks that could cause our results to differ materially from those described in forward-looking statements, please refer to our 2025 Form 10-K, our 2026 10-Qs, and other filings with the SEC. In our earnings supplement, we refer to certain non-GAAP measures.

We believe our non-GAAP measures are more reflective of our cash operations and core business performance. You will find a reconciliation to the equivalent GAAP term in the earnings materials. When used on this call, net revenue refers to revenue net of transaction-based expenses, and adjusted earnings refers to adjusted diluted earnings per share. Throughout this presentation, unless otherwise indicated, references to revenue growth are on a constant currency basis. Please see the explanatory notes on the second page of the earnings supplement for additional details regarding the definition of certain items. Also, we will be discussing our recently announced acquisition of MarketAxess.

The statements made today do not constitute an offer to sell or buy or the solicitation of an offer to sell or buy any securities. With us on the call today are Jeff Sprecher, Chair and CEO; Warren Gardiner, Chief Financial Officer; Ben Jackson, President; Lynn Martin, President of the NYSE; and Chris Edmonds, President of Fixed Income and Data Services. I will now turn over the call to Warren.

Warren Gardiner:Thanks, Steve. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. I will begin on slide 4. Nine months into 2026, our business has been tested by three very different markets. Acute volatility in the first quarter, receding volatility in the second, and in the third, renewed geopolitical risk in global equity, fixed income, and energy markets as rate expectations moved higher across major economies. Each environment was different, and in each one, we grew. A direct result of building a portfolio customers turn to when the world becomes harder to predict.

Third quarter adjusted earnings per share were $2.02, up 18% year-over-year, the best third quarter in our history and the second-best quarter we have ever reported, behind only the first quarter of this year. Net revenues of $2.8 billion were up 15% year-over-year. Adjusted operating income grew 19% to $1.7 billion. Recurring revenues reached a record $1.4 billion, up 7%, and transaction revenues grew 23%. That combination is the engine of the ICE model. Steady compounding at the core and upside operating leverage when our markets are active. Through nine months, adjusted earnings per share of $6.27 are up 20% year-over-year. Adjusted operating expenses were $1,068,000,000, right at the midpoint of our guidance.

As anticipated, the year-over-year increase reflects incentive compensation which tracks with our results, continued investment in product and technology, including our data center and network capacity, and higher depreciation. Importantly, these expenses were offset by better revenues. For the fourth quarter, we expect adjusted operating expenses to be in the range of $1,082,000,000 to $1,092,000,000, which at the midpoint places full-year expenses at the top end of the range we provided in July. Similar to the third quarter, the year-over-year increase is driven by further crystallization of full-year performance-related compensation, investments in both product and technology, as well as higher depreciation.

We expect fourth quarter adjusted non-operating expense to be between $175 million and $185 million, and the adjusted tax rate to be towards the high end of our 24%-26% range. Capital expenditures were $226 million in the quarter and $664 million year-to-date. We now expect full-year CapEx of approximately $1,050,000,000, with the increase relative to July guidance driven largely by our expected fourth quarter purchase of a new campus here in Atlanta, and to a lesser extent, some additional data center and other real estate spend. Adjusted free cash flow was $1.1 billion in the quarter and a record $3.7 billion year-to-date, up 17%.

We repurchased $400 million of stock in the quarter and paid $293 million in dividends, returning $693 million to shareholders. Year-to-date, we've returned $2.5 billion, more than 40% above the same period last year and a record for ICE. During the third quarter, we completed the financing for MarketAxess, issuing $3.75 billion of senior notes. Together with a $2 billion term loan and our commercial paper capacity, the financing is fully in place. Importantly, last week we received approval from the Department of Justice, and as a result, we now expect the transaction to close in the first quarter of 2027, ahead of the first half timeline we outlined in July.

We also repaid approximately $250 million of existing debt in the quarter. Excluding the pre-funded MarketAxess notes, leverage ended the quarter at 2.65 times, down from 2.8x in June and just over 2.9x a year ago. Turning to our segments, starting with exchanges on slide five. Exchanges net revenue was $1.5 billion, up 22%, a third quarter record and nearly 40% above the level of just three years ago. Transaction revenues rose 28%, and every major asset class contributed. Energy grew 26%, interest rates 48%, and agricultural and metal 62%. At the NYSE, cash equities and equity options net revenue grew 25% to $132 million, a third quarter record.

Importantly, total open interest ended the quarter up 13% year-over-year, proving it's a strong foundation as we enter the fourth quarter and look to 2027. Exchange recurring revenues reached a record $422 million, up 8%, and were led by a record $292 million in Exchange Data Services, up 10%, as customers consume more of our futures and equity data across more of their workflows. Our listings franchise continued to attract high-quality companies. Even as industry IPO activity slowed in the third quarter, the NYSE listed the quarter's only two IPOs to raise more than $1 billi```on, Csquare and Jersey Mike's.

Year-to-date, it's facilitated $26.5 billion in IPO proceeds across 73 IPOs, already surpassing all of 2025 and our strongest year since 2021. Nine companies representing nearly half a trillion dollars in market capitalization have also chosen to transfer to the NYSE this year, including AstraZeneca, Fifth Third, Kraft Heinz and Skydance, the largest annual total on record, and our retention rate remains above 99%. Shifting to a few guidance items. Given the strong exchange recurring revenue through the first nine months, we now expect full-year exchange recurring revenue growth of approximately 9%, the upper end of the high single-digit range we discussed in July.

On OTC and other revenues, we anticipate fourth quarter revenues to be around $100 million, driven in part by lower regulatory fees. Moving to Fixed Income and Data Services on slide 6. Fixed Income and Data Services revenues were a record $674 million, up 9% year-over-year. Recurring revenues were a record $538 million, also up 9%. Fixed Income Data and Analytics grew 8% to a record $336 million. Pricing and Reference Data grew 7% on strong consumption trends, net new subscription business, and approximately $3 million of one-time items, while our index business grew 24%. Data network technology revenues grew 10% to a record $202 million, led by demand for low latency connectivity and co-location services.

Transaction revenues grew 11%, led by a record third quarter in CDS clearing, where revenues rose 13% to $102 million. Moving to guidance. This quarter's recurring growth was slightly ahead of the trajectory we outlined in July, driven by stronger consumption trends, net new sales, and growth in index assets. As a result, we now expect full-year FIDS recurring revenue growth of approximately 8%, the top of our prior range. Shifting to Mortgage Technology on slide seven. Mortgage Technology revenues were $549 million, up 4%, with servicing and data and analytics each growing 6%.

Recurring revenues of $405 million grew 4% and increased sequentially once you exclude the roughly $3 million of one-time items we noted in our second quarter results, driven in part by new customers coming online. Transaction revenues also grew 4% in a market that moved against us late in the quarter. This quarter also marks three years since we closed our acquisition on Black Knight, and the integration continues to deliver ahead of plan. We now expect to exit 2026 with approximately $270 million of annualized expense synergies. This compares to an original five-year target of $200 million when we announced the transaction.

Looking to the fourth quarter, while we expect Mortgage Technology recurring revenues to grow modestly from the third quarter, in light of typical fourth quarter seasonality and with mortgage rates elevated, we expect transaction revenues to decline from both the third quarter and the prior year. Through 9 months, ICE has grown adjusted earnings per share 20% on 12% revenue growth while expanding margins, accelerating investment, delivering a record return of capital to shareholders, and making several strategic investments across our business.

Our growth is driven by benchmarks that the world relies on to price energy and interest rate risk, and data and network services that are becoming core infrastructure for super intelligence or AI-driven workflows across fixed income and mortgages. I will be happy to take your questions during Q&A, but for now, I will turn it over to Ben.

Ben Jackson:Thank you, Warren, and thank you all for joining us this morning. Please turn to slide 8. Several structural forces continue to reshape markets at the same time. Energy supply chains are being rebuilt. Central banks are evolving in different directions. Europe is investing heavily in defense, energy security, and infrastructure. AI is creating new demands for power, compute, and data. Each of those trends create uncertainty. Our customers need tools to price risk, transfer risk, and manage that uncertainty, and they increasingly rely on ICE's markets, data, and technology to do it. That dynamic was evident again this quarter.

Futures and options average daily volume was up 31%, a record for any third quarter and our second highest quarter ever, while total open interest finished the quarter up 13%. That momentum has carried into the fourth quarter, with volume up 13% quarter to-date. Customers aren't just trading more with us, they are also managing more risk with us. There is plenty of debate about how quickly energy demand will grow. What matters for our markets is that customers are managing a wider range of potential outcomes than they were in the past. On a year-to-date basis, our energy revenues compounded 12% annually over the last decade, while global electricity demand grew by less than 3% per year.

The risk the world needs to manage has grown much faster than the energy it consumes. If energy demand grows faster over the next decade, as the IEA and many others expect, due to AI and industrialization, that is potentially significant upside for our energy business. This is a time where a liquid benchmark matters most because customers need the ability to adjust positions as conditions change. Look at Europe as an example. The European Union now imports nearly 90% of the natural gas it consumes, helping turn TTF into a global benchmark.

Europe has spent the last several years rebuilding its gas supply chain away from Russian gas, while Asia and the Middle East are establishing new supply chains following disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. There are more hydrocarbons in transit on more routes, more of the time, creating more exposures that need to be hedged. Independent forecasts project global LNG liquefaction capacity increasing by roughly 40% by 2030. As new supply enters the market and trade flows continue to evolve, customers need tools to manage a growing network of pricing relationships that increasingly run through ICE benchmarks. The third quarter put those forces on full display. Qatari LNG exports remained under force majeure.

All three principal LNG routes into Europe were disrupted at one point in the summer, and Europe entered the heating season with storage nearly 20% less than the five-year average. Customers responded by coming to our benchmarks. In the quarter, TTF volume increased 39% year-over-year. TTF options volume rose 72%, and participation grew double digits to a record. JKM volume increased by 45%, and futures OI hit a record in August, while Brent volume was up 38% and participation grew high single digits. We built our platform for exactly this environment. Benchmark contracts at key intersections of geography and energy type, supported by the regional contracts, differentials, and spreads customers use to hedge risk through a single clearinghouse.

Open interest and participation remain the clearest indicators of the health of our markets because they show whether customers are building and keeping positions with us. Energy OI ended the quarter at 66 million lots, with options OI up 14%. Options represent 40% of energy OI and have more than doubled since the third quarter of 2021, reflecting growing customer demand to manage complex and longer-dated risk. Capital efficiency continues to reinforce that growth. ICE Risk Model 2, or IRM2, return meaningful margin to customers, freeing capital they can put back to work in our markets. Alongside those changes in global energy trade flows, data centers are creating a new location-specific source of energy demand.

The IEA projects U.S. electricity demand growing roughly twice as fast through 2030 as it did over the previous decade. We don't need to predict how quickly they're built or which molecule fuels them. Whether projects accelerate or slow, our customers still need to manage the resulting power and natural gas exposures. If history is any guide, acceleration of electricity demand should lead to compounding additional growth in our corresponding power, gas, and environmental markets, enabling clients to trade the full clean spark spread in one place. That demand reaches our markets through both grid expansion and on-site power generation.

Utilities building capacity increasingly touch our power markets, while operators installing gas turbines near pipelines rely on natural gas basis markets we operate to manage fuel costs. We're already seeing it. Our North American financial gas markets delivered their strongest third quarter on record, with volume up 15% and OI reaching a record of 13.4 million lots on July 1st. LNG export demand, new permanent pipeline capacity, summer heat, and data center development are all creating greater regional basis risk, driving activity across our network of over 70 North American gas hubs, all exclusive to ICE.

Beyond power, AI is also creating demand for compute itself, and we see an opportunity to bring to it the same market structure that has supported energy for decades, transparent pricing and risk management tools. The volatility across AI infrastructure this year shows why. GPU rental rates can rise when capacity is scarce or fall as new supply comes online. Trusted indices and forward curves give builders, operators, and investors a way to manage the price in both directions and over time, lower the cost of capital behind it. We're pursuing that opportunity through two partnerships.

The Ornn Index tracks the rental price of specific chips, while the NATIVX COIL Index is energy normalized and designed to trade alongside our natural gas and power futures. Subject to regulatory review, together, they will give customers a single platform and clearing relationship to manage both the energy required to produce intelligence and the compute required to deliver it. Agricultural markets also delivered a strong quarter, with volumes up 57% and open interest up 43%, including record sugar OI of 2.5 million lots on September 11. The same demand for risk management is evident in our financials franchise. Europe is entering a multi-year investment cycle in defense, energy security, and infrastructure. Much of it is financed through government borrowing.

This creates additional demand to manage euro and sterling rate risk on ICE. EURIBOR and €STR in the Euro area, SONIA and Gilts in the U.K. At the same time, higher energy prices push central banks back toward tightening. When rate expectations move, customers come to ICE to manage that risk. This quarter, interest rate volume increased 49%, with EURIBOR up 40% and SONIA up 63%. Activity accelerated further in September, with total rate volume up 95%, EURIBOR up 84%, and SONIA up 119%. More risk is being managed at ICE than ever before. On September 10, we set records for futures OI in both financials at 17.5 million lots and interest rates at 15 million lots.

Interest rate OI finished the quarter up 30%. EURIBOR futures OI reached a record 6 million lots, and SONIA OI was up 48%. Central banks are moving on different paths globally, and customers can manage that rate risk across currencies and tenors from a single capital-efficient venue. Clearing futures and options together provide meaningful offsets, and capital efficiencies tend to drive additional activity. This month, we extended IRM2 to our rates franchise at ICE Clear Europe, further enhancing those benefits for our customers. Together, these dynamics continue to drive more risk management through our markets and reinforce the strength of our financials franchise. Please turn to slide nine.

The same borrowing driving activity in our rates markets is also expanding the universe of debt that must be priced, valued, and indexed every day. When credit markets reprice, clients rely more heavily on independent pricing and credit protection. We've seen that throughout the year. During the September index roll, ICE Clear Credit cleared $2.7 trillion of notional in a single day, and CDS clearing revenue grew 13%, its strongest third quarter on record. Much of fixed income has no continuously observable price, which is why our evaluated pricing, covering millions of securities every day, is the foundation for indices, analytics, and risk management workflows.

Around it sits a connected network of data, execution, and post-trade services, and every interaction adds to the proprietary data we own. Once the transaction closes, we expect to extend that network through the MarketAxess platform, which serves more than 2,100 client firms. Those network effects help drive another record quarter of recurring revenue. Because our indices are built on our own evaluated pricing, every new security we price can become a constituent in a benchmark. ETF assets benchmarked to ICE indices reached a record $935 billion, up 24%. We're taking the same path into private credit, a market that has grown quickly while the data infrastructure beneath it hasn't.

In July, with Apollo as our anchor partner, we launched ICE IDs, the first foundational identifiers for private credit. In September, we added a reference data service on top of them, giving private credit the same infrastructure that public markets rely on. Demand for proximity to markets also keeps growing. Trading firms, and increasingly the AI-driven models they run, need to sit next to matching engines and data sources, and we sell that capacity through forward options that give us visibility into demand years out. We've doubled our global co-location capacity since 2020, and with our new data center, we're set to double it again.

AI may commoditize models and interfaces, but not the proprietary data, methodology, context, and permissions behind them, such as the evaluated prices for securities that rarely trade and can't easily be scraped from the internet. So we're meeting clients where they're moving, delivering our data through an MCP on an open standard built to work across AI platforms. Clients pay for the value of the data, not the compute, so our economics are tied to the data, not to which model wins. Please turn to slide 10. In Mortgage Technology, our data does more than inform decisions because it sits inside the network of record for U.S. housing finance, where those decisions are carried out.

A mortgage changes hands many times over its life, from lender to closing agent, to servicer, to investor. Our network connects participants at each step, including roughly 3,000 lenders and more than 80,000 notaries. Encompass, MERS, and MSP are the systems of record where those handoffs take place. So loan data travels with the loan rather than being pulled out and re-audited at every stage. That lowers costs for customers who run more of the life cycle with us, and every new participant makes the network more valuable for those already on it. That network continues to deepen.

Wells Fargo renewed its MSP agreement, extending a relationship of more than 35 years, and is moving its home equity portfolio onto MSP while also using ICE Business Intelligence. Freedom Mortgage signed onto MSP for its HELOC portfolio, bringing us to five new MSP clients year-to-date. Meanwhile, clients keep building on our platforms with our servicing business processing 11.6 billion API and web services calls in the quarter, up 36%. Inside those systems of record, we and our customers are putting AI to work in two ways.

First, our agents embedded in Encompass and MSP automate workflows that lower the cost to originate and service the loan and increase capacity for our clients with a human in the loop on exceptions in every step, fully auditable. Second, as in FIDS, starting this quarter, customers will be able to deploy their own agents connecting to either Encompass or MSP through a Model Context Protocol in a fully auditable way, and several of our clients are already engaging with us on this. Those agents work where the data, permissions, and audit trail already live. An agent can draft text in seconds, but acting on a mortgage takes trusted loan data and regulatory controls.

That's why every agent working inside MSP or Encompass makes the system of record more valuable. With roughly half of U.S. loans on Encompass and MSP and 85% on MERS, our agents learn from a view of the market that's hard to replicate, and we hold them to the same standard as the rest of our critical infrastructure with internal audits confirming our alignment with GSE rules and independent assessments, including from EY, validating our governance and controls. Stepping back, the third quarter proved what our networks do when the world needs more risk managed, more securities priced, and more workflows automated.

Customers manage record risk in our rates markets, extended their hedges across our energy curves, put more of our data to work in their SI workflows, and deepened their use of our mortgage network. Whichever way these trends break, they run through our networks and every new participant, position, and data point makes those networks more valuable for the next. With that, I'll hand it over to Jeff.

Jeff Sprecher:Thank you, Ben. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Please turn to slide 11. Since the pandemic, we've seen a clear rise in retail participation in markets, and that participation is becoming far more global. Increasingly, retail traders seek short-duration exposures with the ability to move in and out of positions quickly, often around the clock. This trend gained attention with digital assets, but now extends well beyond crypto into equities, commodities, foreign exchange, and other real-world assets. And it's growing in conjunction with the institutional risk management growth that remains at the core of our markets. We see this trend as an expansion of our opportunity set for risk transfer and price discovery.

ICE has historically been a business-to-business company built for commercial hedgers, institutional investors, and other sophisticated market participants. Our futures product suite was designed around the risk management needs of those customers, which is why their composition is more than 99% institutional. Consider an electric utility in Asia contracting today for LNG cargoes that won't arrive until next year. To price the electric power that it will sell, the utility needs confidence in what that gas will cost when these LNG cargoes land. That's why utilities rely on our futures markets to lock in prices for specific settlement dates along a forward pricing curve, and why our customers tend to hold such positions for the long term.

As we shared last quarter, more than half of the open interest across our energy markets is over six months in duration, and these long-term commitments are reflected in the global scale of our markets. The perpetual futures market serves a different purpose. Because a perp contract never expires, it does not lock in a price for future dates. Instead, it facilitates short-term exposure. This distinction clearly shows up in perpetual futures trading behavior. According to data published by the Pyth Network, the average holding period for a perpetual oil futures contract in September was just 12 hours, a hold much shorter than a single day and even shorter than a traditional financial settlement cycle.

We see these perp markets as additive to our futures markets, not a replacement for them. That brings us to our recently announced agreement with Trade[XYZ], under which ICE becomes the exclusive operator of Trade[XYZ]'s regulated markets alongside a strategic investment in the company. Trade[XYZ] has become a leading deployer of real-world asset perpetual markets on the Hyperliquid blockchain, one of the largest decentralized derivative trading platforms, and one that has attracted significant global retail participation. Hyperliquid manages the underlying technology for Trade[XYZ], much like Pillar for the New York Stock Exchange, while Trade[XYZ] designs the products that customers seek to trade.

Together with Trade[XYZ] and subject to regulatory approvals, we intend to bring these markets into a U.S. regulated framework by combining Trade[XYZ]'s retail market expertise with ICE's exchange, clearing, and regulatory capabilities. Once approved, verified customers are expected to access Hyperliquid-based markets through futures commission merchants that will now perform Know Your Customer and anti-money laundering screening, including distribution via our joint venture FCM with OKX. This retail-oriented, blockchain-based Trade[XYZ] business will operate separately from our institutional futures and clearing franchise. Commercial hedgers can continue to rely on customary futures markets, our forward pricing curves, and established trading and clearing infrastructure.

The retail perpetual futures opportunity will deploy blockchain technology and serve a customer base with unique trading and settlement demands. Earlier this year, we made a strategic investment in OKX, which has a global customer base of over 120 million accounts. We have since announced a joint venture, pending regulatory approval, that would provide a regulated framework for connecting this global retail customer base to securities and commodities listed on ICE and the New York Stock Exchange legacy technology platforms. As we build out this OKX joint venture, we believe communication and transparency will be critical to the development of the tokenized securities markets.

This applies to our joint venture's tokenized securities venue, now known as a TSV, which will operate using OKX's wallet and its X Layer blockchain. We have chosen to publicize the securities identified for tokenization, and we have elected to maintain an ongoing dialogue with issuers as this tokenized market develops. Some issuers have chosen not to participate initially, but we believe our engagement and transparency will help build the trust needed for tokenized markets to digitize within this newly regulated environment. With OKX and Trade[XYZ], we now have relationships with two preeminent blockchain ecosystems. OKX's centralized and DeFi blockchain platforms, and with Hyperliquid, where its HIP-3 blockchain framework allows builders like Trade[XYZ] to deploy markets.

Our investment in Trade[XYZ] complements what we are building with OKX. Each of these relationships plays its own role in a broader ecosystem. OKX provides distribution and access to ICE's existing platforms using its KYC and AML-compliant wallet technology. Trade[XYZ] brings expertise in retail perpetual markets on the Hyperliquid blockchain, and ICE provides the regulated risk management oversight that ties them together. With our relationship with Polymarket, we are bringing crowdsourced probability assessments into institutional workflows, turning prediction market data into a new source of signals that complement traditional Pricing and Reference Data sources. We also continue to evolve traditional markets across ICE.

At the New York Stock Exchange, we have introduced extended trading hours on our options markets and are looking forward to launching 23x5 trading on equities in December, an industry initiative that we have long led. We continue developing products that help customers manage event-driven risks, including our Binary Return Derivatives, known as ByRDs, and binary options tied to key performance indicators, known as KPIs, both of which have now received necessary regulatory approvals. We have also introduced economic indicator futures tied to both central bank rate decisions and U.S. natural gas storage reports, giving customers exchange-traded, centrally cleared instruments to express views on specific market-moving economic events.

To support enhanced risk management and greater trading activity outside of traditional banking hours, we are partnering with our key global settlement banks to allow for commercial bank deposits to be moved to meet margin calls during weekends and holidays. As markets evolve, participants still need to trust the price, trust the counterparty, and trust capital moving when needed. That trust is what ICE has spent decades building, and it is what we bring to every new market we serve while continuing to strengthen the institutional franchise at the core of our business. Our strategy remains consistent. We invest behind long-term trends that expand participation, increase transparency, and create new demand for our markets and data.

Applied with discipline over time, that strategy compounds, delivering growth on top of growth in varying environments. I would like to end our prepared remarks by thanking our customers for their business and their continued trust, and by thanking my colleagues at ICE, whose execution contributed to the best third quarter and the best year-to-date performance in our company's history. I will now turn the call back to our moderator, Jade, to conduct the question and answer section until 9:30 A.M. Eastern Time.

Operator:Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. Please limit yourself to one question. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. To withdraw your question, press star one again. We ask that you pick up your handset when asking a question, and if you are muted locally, please remember to unmute your device. Please stand by while we compile the Q&A roster. Your first question comes from the line of Patrick Moley from Piper Sandler. Please go ahead.

Patrick Moley:Yes, good morning. Jeff, just wanted to follow up on the Trade[XYZ] investment. You laid out the strategic logic there, so I'm more interested in how your view on real-world asset perpetuals as an asset class has maybe evolved over the last few months, and which underlying do you think are most relevant for a U.S. retail audience? Separately, I think a lot of people in this space know Trade[XYZ] as the platform that got the official S&P 500 license for a perpetual contract. So maybe just how important was that license in this decision, and is that a contract that you think you can help them bring onshore? Thanks.

Jeff Sprecher:Thanks for the question. I think stepping back, we heard about Hyperliquid, oh gosh, well more than a year ago. Really just heard about its technology features. And we were able to track them down in Singapore and I actually had a meeting with them well over a year ago to talk about working together. But I was invited to a press conference in the White House and the President actually asked me to stand next to him when he was talking about the crypto bill. As he was doing the weave, I looked over and saw his script that he was going to talk about Hyperliquid.

Honestly, in that moment, I said, "Okay, the U.S. wants this platform to come and be regulated in this country." So we redoubled our efforts to bring both founder groups together, both Trade[XYZ] and Hyperliquid to work with us. These markets, as I mentioned in the prepared remarks, we believe are complementary. Because they don't have a forward pricing curve, they're very good short-term investments. They are used by more than retail for very short-term periods. And we think it's complementary to what we do and that we shouldn't ignore them. As I mentioned, the U.S. government is going to bring these markets onshore and seek to regulate them, which is something we know a lot about.

In terms of which assets will go and what indexes will be on there, that's really up to Trade[XYZ]. We're working with them on a number of different things in the background and have been for quite some time. But we need to get our regulatory approval and see what the CFTC is willing to allow. Right now, perps are largely just crypto related. But again, I'm taking a cue from the White House that our regulators don't want U.S. clients using VPNs to trade these markets unregulated overseas. So I'm sure that regulatory compact will evolve as we go forward.

Patrick Moley:All right. Great color, Jeff, and congrats on the quarter.

Jeff Sprecher:Thank you very much.

Operator:Your next question comes from the line of Alex Blostein from Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Blostein:Hey, Jeff. Good morning, everybody as well. I wanted to ask you guys a question around fixed income data business. We have seen multiple quarters now of above-trend growth. You got it to 8% for the full year for FIDS. Taking a step back, what do you think has changed in the trajectory that you have seen relative to the last couple of years? What has been driving that? How durable do you think that ultimately is? If we could also perhaps incorporate how maybe some of the AI and agentic-related demands for data could further enhance growth in this business, that would be helpful. Thanks.

Chris Edmonds:Hey, Alex, it's Chris. Thanks for the question. What I would say, and I said it a couple of quarters ago around client focus on making sure that they have the right vendors lined up. What is clear across the customer base at the moment is they're looking for fewer number of vendors that can provide them greater level of scale along the way. We've been able to do that, and I think that's what you're seeing in the growth that we've shown in FIDS over the last few quarters.

We continue to focus on that to make sure that we have the right data assets, the right place delivered in a way that they need to engage as their businesses continue to evolve on a go-forward basis. It's really more of that saying, it's amazing if you listen to what your customers are telling you and you can deliver that output, it tends to go pretty well. Ben Jackson:Thank you, Warren, and thank you all for joining us this morning. Please turn to slide 8. Several structural forces continue to reshape markets at the same time. Energy supply chains are being rebuilt. Central banks are evolving in different directions. Europe is investing heavily in defense, energy security, and infrastructure. AI is creating new demands for power, compute, and data. Each of those trends create uncertainty. Our customers need tools to price risk, transfer risk, and manage that uncertainty, and they increasingly rely on ICE's markets, data, and technology to do it. That dynamic was evident again this quarter.

Futures and options average daily volume was up 31%, a record for any third quarter and our second highest quarter ever, while total open interest finished the quarter up 13%. That momentum has carried into the fourth quarter, with volume up 13% quarter to-date. Customers aren't just trading more with us, they are also managing more risk with us. There is plenty of debate about how quickly energy demand will grow. What matters for our markets is that customers are managing a wider range of potential outcomes than they were in the past. On a year-to-date basis, our energy revenues compounded 12% annually over the last decade, while global electricity demand grew by less than 3% per year.

The risk the world needs to manage has grown much faster than the energy it consumes. If energy demand grows faster over the next decade, as the IEA and many others expect, due to AI and industrialization, that is potentially significant upside for our energy business. This is a time where a liquid benchmark matters most because customers need the ability to adjust positions as conditions change. Look at Europe as an example. The European Union now imports nearly 90% of the natural gas it consumes, helping turn TTF into a global benchmark.

Europe has spent the last several years rebuilding its gas supply chain away from Russian gas, while Asia and the Middle East are establishing new supply chains following disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. There are more hydrocarbons in transit on more routes, more of the time, creating more exposures that need to be hedged. Independent forecasts project global LNG liquefaction capacity increasing by roughly 40% by 2030. As new supply enters the market and trade flows continue to evolve, customers need tools to manage a growing network of pricing relationships that increasingly run through ICE benchmarks. The third quarter put those forces on full display. Qatari LNG exports remained under force majeure.

All three principal LNG routes into Europe were disrupted at one point in the summer, and Europe entered the heating season with storage nearly 20% less than the five-year average. Customers responded by coming to our benchmarks. In the quarter, TTF volume increased 39% year-over-year. TTF options volume rose 72%, and participation grew double digits to a record. JKM volume increased by 45%, and futures OI hit a record in August, while Brent volume was up 38% and participation grew high single digits. We built our platform for exactly this environment. Benchmark contracts at key intersections of geography and energy type, supported by the regional contracts, differentials, and spreads customers use to hedge risk through a single clearinghouse.

Open interest and participation remain the clearest indicators of the health of our markets because they show whether customers are building and keeping positions with us. Energy OI ended the quarter at 66 million lots, with options OI up 14%. Options represent 40% of energy OI and have more than doubled since the third quarter of 2021, reflecting growing customer demand to manage complex and longer-dated risk. Capital efficiency continues to reinforce that growth. ICE Risk Model 2, or IRM2, return meaningful margin to customers, freeing capital they can put back to work in our markets. Alongside those changes in global energy trade flows, data centers are creating a new location-specific source of energy demand.

The IEA projects U.S. electricity demand growing roughly twice as fast through 2030 as it did over the previous decade. We don't need to predict how quickly they're built or which molecule fuels them. Whether projects accelerate or slow, our customers still need to manage the resulting power and natural gas exposures. If history is any guide, acceleration of electricity demand should lead to compounding additional growth in our corresponding power, gas, and environmental markets, enabling clients to trade the full clean spark spread in one place. That demand reaches our markets through both grid expansion and on-site power generation.

Utilities building capacity increasingly touch our power markets, while operators installing gas turbines near pipelines rely on natural gas basis markets we operate to manage fuel costs. We're already seeing it. Our North American financial gas markets delivered their strongest third quarter on record, with volume up 15% and OI reaching a record of 13.4 million lots on July 1st. LNG export demand, new permanent pipeline capacity, summer heat, and data center development are all creating greater regional basis risk, driving activity across our network of over 70 North American gas hubs, all exclusive to ICE.

Beyond power, AI is also creating demand for compute itself, and we see an opportunity to bring to it the same market structure that has supported energy for decades, transparent pricing and risk management tools. The volatility across AI infrastructure this year shows why. GPU rental rates can rise when capacity is scarce or fall as new supply comes online. Trusted indices and forward curves give builders, operators, and investors a way to manage the price in both directions and over time, lower the cost of capital behind it. We're pursuing that opportunity through two partnerships.

The Ornn Index tracks the rental price of specific chips, while the NATIVX COIL Index is energy normalized and designed to trade alongside our natural gas and power futures. Subject to regulatory review, together, they will give customers a single platform and clearing relationship to manage both the energy required to produce intelligence and the compute required to deliver it. Agricultural markets also delivered a strong quarter, with volumes up 57% and open interest up 43%, including record sugar OI of 2.5 million lots on September 11. The same demand for risk management is evident in our financials franchise. Europe is entering a multi-year investment cycle in defense, energy security, and infrastructure. Much of it is financed through government borrowing.

This creates additional demand to manage euro and sterling rate risk on ICE. EURIBOR and €STR in the Euro area, SONIA and Gilts in the U.K. At the same time, higher energy prices push central banks back toward tightening. When rate expectations move, customers come to ICE to manage that risk. This quarter, interest rate volume increased 49%, with EURIBOR up 40% and SONIA up 63%. Activity accelerated further in September, with total rate volume up 95%, EURIBOR up 84%, and SONIA up 119%. More risk is being managed at ICE than ever before. On September 10, we set records for futures OI in both financials at 17.5 million lots and interest rates at 15 million lots.

Interest rate OI finished the quarter up 30%. EURIBOR futures OI reached a record 6 million lots, and SONIA OI was up 48%. Central banks are moving on different paths globally, and customers can manage that rate risk across currencies and tenors from a single capital-efficient venue. Clearing futures and options together provide meaningful offsets, and capital efficiencies tend to drive additional activity. This month, we extended IRM2 to our rates franchise at ICE Clear Europe, further enhancing those benefits for our customers. Together, these dynamics continue to drive more risk management through our markets and reinforce the strength of our financials franchise. Please turn to slide nine.

The same borrowing driving activity in our rates markets is also expanding the universe of debt that must be priced, valued, and indexed every day. When credit markets reprice, clients rely more heavily on independent pricing and credit protection. We've seen that throughout the year. During the September index roll, ICE Clear Credit cleared $2.7 trillion of notional in a single day, and CDS clearing revenue grew 13%, its strongest third quarter on record. Much of fixed income has no continuously observable price, which is why our evaluated pricing, covering millions of securities every day, is the foundation for indices, analytics, and risk management workflows.

Around it sits a connected network of data, execution, and post-trade services, and every interaction adds to the proprietary data we own. Once the transaction closes, we expect to extend that network through the MarketAxess platform, which serves more than 2,100 client firms. Those network effects help drive another record quarter of recurring revenue. Because our indices are built on our own evaluated pricing, every new security we price can become a constituent in a benchmark. ETF assets benchmarked to ICE indices reached a record $935 billion, up 24%. We're taking the same path into private credit, a market that has grown quickly while the data infrastructure beneath it hasn't.

In July, with Apollo as our anchor partner, we launched ICE IDs, the first foundational identifiers for private credit. In September, we added a reference data service on top of them, giving private credit the same infrastructure that public markets rely on. Demand for proximity to markets also keeps growing. Trading firms, and increasingly the AI-driven models they run, need to sit next to matching engines and data sources, and we sell that capacity through forward options that give us visibility into demand years out. We've doubled our global co-location capacity since 2020, and with our new data center, we're set to double it again.

AI may commoditize models and interfaces, but not the proprietary data, methodology, context, and permissions behind them, such as the evaluated prices for securities that rarely trade and can't easily be scraped from the internet. So we're meeting clients where they're moving, delivering our data through an MCP on an open standard built to work across AI platforms. Clients pay for the value of the data, not the compute, so our economics are tied to the data, not to which model wins. Please turn to slide 10. In Mortgage Technology, our data does more than inform decisions because it sits inside the network of record for U.S. housing finance, where those decisions are carried out.

A mortgage changes hands many times over its life, from lender to closing agent, to servicer, to investor. Our network connects participants at each step, including roughly 3,000 lenders and more than 80,000 notaries. Encompass, MERS, and MSP are the systems of record where those handoffs take place. So loan data travels with the loan rather than being pulled out and re-audited at every stage. That lowers costs for customers who run more of the life cycle with us, and every new participant makes the network more valuable for those already on it. That network continues to deepen.

Wells Fargo renewed its MSP agreement, extending a relationship of more than 35 years, and is moving its home equity portfolio onto MSP while also using ICE Business Intelligence. Freedom Mortgage signed onto MSP for its HELOC portfolio, bringing us to five new MSP clients year-to-date. Meanwhile, clients keep building on our platforms with our servicing business processing 11.6 billion API and web services calls in the quarter, up 36%. Inside those systems of record, we and our customers are putting AI to work in two ways.

First, our agents embedded in Encompass and MSP automate workflows that lower the cost to originate and service the loan and increase capacity for our clients with a human in the loop on exceptions in every step, fully auditable. Second, as in FIDS, starting this quarter, customers will be able to deploy their own agents connecting to either Encompass or MSP through a Model Context Protocol in a fully auditable way, and several of our clients are already engaging with us on this. Those agents work where the data, permissions, and audit trail already live. An agent can draft text in seconds, but acting on a mortgage takes trusted loan data and regulatory controls.

That's why every agent working inside MSP or Encompass makes the system of record more valuable. With roughly half of U.S. loans on Encompass and MSP and 85% on MERS, our agents learn from a view of the market that's hard to replicate, and we hold them to the same standard as the rest of our critical infrastructure with internal audits confirming our alignment with GSE rules and independent assessments, including from EY, validating our governance and controls. Stepping back, the third quarter proved what our networks do when the world needs more risk managed, more securities priced, and more workflows automated.

Customers manage record risk in our rates markets, extended their hedges across our energy curves, put more of our data to work in their SI workflows, and deepened their use of our mortgage network. Whichever way these trends break, they run through our networks and every new participant, position, and data point makes those networks more valuable for the next. With that, I'll hand it over to Jeff.

Jeff Sprecher:Thank you, Ben. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Please turn to slide 11. Since the pandemic, we've seen a clear rise in retail participation in markets, and that participation is becoming far more global. Increasingly, retail traders seek short-duration exposures with the ability to move in and out of positions quickly, often around the clock. This trend gained attention with digital assets, but now extends well beyond crypto into equities, commodities, foreign exchange, and other real-world assets. And it's growing in conjunction with the institutional risk management growth that remains at the core of our markets. We see this trend as an expansion of our opportunity set for risk transfer and price discovery.

ICE has historically been a business-to-business company built for commercial hedgers, institutional investors, and other sophisticated market participants. Our futures product suite was designed around the risk management needs of those customers, which is why their composition is more than 99% institutional. Consider an electric utility in Asia contracting today for LNG cargoes that won't arrive until next year. To price the electric power that it will sell, the utility needs confidence in what that gas will cost when these LNG cargoes land. That's why utilities rely on our futures markets to lock in prices for specific settlement dates along a forward pricing curve, and why our customers tend to hold such positions for the long term.

As we shared last quarter, more than half of the open interest across our energy markets is over six months in duration, and these long-term commitments are reflected in the global scale of our markets. The perpetual futures market serves a different purpose. Because a perp contract never expires, it does not lock in a price for future dates. Instead, it facilitates short-term exposure. This distinction clearly shows up in perpetual futures trading behavior. According to data published by the Pyth Network, the average holding period for a perpetual oil futures contract in September was just 12 hours, a hold much shorter than a single day and even shorter than a traditional financial settlement cycle.

We see these perp markets as additive to our futures markets, not a replacement for them. That brings us to our recently announced agreement with Trade[XYZ], under which ICE becomes the exclusive operator of Trade[XYZ]'s regulated markets alongside a strategic investment in the company. Trade[XYZ] has become a leading deployer of real-world asset perpetual markets on the Hyperliquid blockchain, one of the largest decentralized derivative trading platforms, and one that has attracted significant global retail participation. Hyperliquid manages the underlying technology for Trade[XYZ], much like Pillar for the New York Stock Exchange, while Trade[XYZ] designs the products that customers seek to trade.

Together with Trade[XYZ] and subject to regulatory approvals, we intend to bring these markets into a U.S. regulated framework by combining Trade[XYZ]'s retail market expertise with ICE's exchange, clearing, and regulatory capabilities. Once approved, verified customers are expected to access Hyperliquid-based markets through futures commission merchants that will now perform Know Your Customer and anti-money laundering screening, including distribution via our joint venture FCM with OKX. This retail-oriented, blockchain-based Trade[XYZ] business will operate separately from our institutional futures and clearing franchise. Commercial hedgers can continue to rely on customary futures markets, our forward pricing curves, and established trading and clearing infrastructure.

The retail perpetual futures opportunity will deploy blockchain technology and serve a customer base with unique trading and settlement demands. Earlier this year, we made a strategic investment in OKX, which has a global customer base of over 120 million accounts. We have since announced a joint venture, pending regulatory approval, that would provide a regulated framework for connecting this global retail customer base to securities and commodities listed on ICE and the New York Stock Exchange legacy technology platforms. As we build out this OKX joint venture, we believe communication and transparency will be critical to the development of the tokenized securities markets.

This applies to our joint venture's tokenized securities venue, now known as a TSV, which will operate using OKX's wallet and its X Layer blockchain. We have chosen to publicize the securities identified for tokenization, and we have elected to maintain an ongoing dialogue with issuers as this tokenized market develops. Some issuers have chosen not to participate initially, but we believe our engagement and transparency will help build the trust needed for tokenized markets to digitize within this newly regulated environment.
